concepts.def: Rotating y=f(x) around the x-axis from a to b: V = π∫ₐᵇ y² dx.

walkthroughs.h2: Volume from y=x between 0 and 2 about x-axis
walkthroughs.body_html:
y² = x²

V = π∫₀² x² dx = π[x³/3]₀² = 8π/3

walkthroughs.h2: Volume from y=√x between 0 and 4 about x-axis
walkthroughs.body_html:
y² = x

V = π∫₀⁴ x dx = π[x²/2]₀⁴ = 8π

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of a constant, like d/dx(5)?
options: The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
The derivative of 5 is 5 because the constant stays the same.
0 — constants do not change with x.
Definite integrals are negative only when the limits are reversed.

mcqs.q: Can a definite integral give a negative value, even when integrating a function from left to right?
options: Definite integrals are negative only when the limits are reversed.
Yes — if the function is below the x-axis over the interval, the integral is negative.
The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
Definite integrals are always positive because area cannot be negative.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of (3x + 1)^2 with respect to x?
options: The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
The derivative is 9x^2 + 6x + 1 by leaving it as it is.
6(3x + 1) — by the chain rule, multiplying by the derivative of the inside (3).
The derivative is 2(3x + 1) — applying the power rule without the chain rule.
